verse.reading: If you go about cherishing desire for women, there is no way left to set your desire on heaven, stony mind.
verse.nuance: The second of three desires named in 1790 to 1793: land (rule), women and gold, the stock triad of the Siddhars. விண்ணாசை, desire for the sky, is the one desire that is allowed.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: It is always rock salt in this body of eight spans; what is the reason that, seeing it, they do not know it? Always the moon: drawing off that urine, setting it on fire and heating it, I realise the truth as strength.
verse.nuance: அமுரி is the Siddha medical word for urine, used in rejuvenation (amuri karpam), and இந்துப்பு (rock salt) is tied to இந்து, the moon, by sound. The verse claims the body already holds the substance (எண்சாண் உடல், the eight-span body) and that heating it gives strength; a coded reading takes the moon's fluid as the nectar from the head. This is a claim about a substance, recorded as history, not as a remedy.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: Seeking food for the belly in every place where someone will give it, when shall I now stop this fretful wandering?
verse.nuance: கும்பி is the belly as a pot. The stanza is against the renouncer's own begging round, not against householders' giving; the fault is வெம்பித் திரிகை, roaming in distress for food.

finding.claim: Intermittent fasting improves metabolic markers in animals and some humans, but trials show weight loss similar to ordinary calorie restriction.

tamil: பின் இரண்டு சங்கிலிக்குள் பிணிப்பது இனி எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will I bind the twelve-legged horse that leaps, so that it does not kick the plate, within the two chains behind?
verse.nuance: A cipher verse. The horse with twelve legs is the breath (Tirumular's ஈராறு கால் புரவி), its twelve being the twelve finger-breadths the breath travels or the twelve kalas; the two chains behind are, in the tradition, ida and pingala, or the two nostrils; சில்லம் is unexplained (a shard, a wheel, a plate). The plain sense is a wild horse tethered; the cipher makes it the breath held.

finding.claim: Nasal breathing entrains oscillations in olfactory and limbic brain areas and improves memory and fear recognition timed to inhalation, an effect absent with mouth breathing.

verse.reading: Blow the flute, herdsman, saying that dogs that are never tied are never fit for guarding.
verse.nuance: The argument of 1832 completed: restraint is what makes the senses useful. The claim is not that the senses are evil but that unleashed they cannot do the one thing a dog is for.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: Not able to know the nature of the ida and pingala channels, the poet says he hesitated with obstruction.
verse.nuance: இடை and பிங்கலை are the left and right channels, sun and moon in the Siddhar cipher; இயல்பு, their nature, is their alternation, which the Tirumanthiram's வாரசரம் chapter teaches. தடை, obstruction, and தயங்கினேன், hesitated, describe a breath that would not move: the loss is in the practice itself.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: In the root of the hard-to-reach Paramasiva, the place where the two lights rise and set; the sushumna, where the body's working ceases, becoming the pillar, stands settled as the light that is the true thing; in this way, worship the foot called the root at the place where the two times are no more, and see.
verse.nuance: இருசுடர், the two lights, are sun and moon, which in the cipher are the right and left breaths; the sushumna is where they rise and sink. இருநேரம் அற்றிடம், the place without the two times, may mean beyond day and night or beyond the two breaths. The first two lines are printed twice with small variants, which looks like a doubled couplet.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: After praising the Lord of Pugali whose fame shone in the twelve ages past under different names, the bull-rider, husband of Uma, who bent the mountain and burnt the three cities of the strong-shouldered demons, with young moon on his growing hair and the single eye in his forehead that glared at Kama, the beginning the gods do not know, the poet confesses: in my untaught heart base understanding followed me, and with the empty gaze that looks and forgets, each time I looked, everything everywhere, mine and others', the many that come to be and the many that perish, what goes, comes and passes, more numerous than the sand heaped in the clear-watered world, the non-existent seeming to be and the existent unseen, I lay for many days in darkness; and the way it shook me was like a man who cannot see with his eyes and reels, the pit becoming his road and the road a pit, stumbling without end from one into the other; so it came, until I gained by compassion your look of growing grace, and then everything appeared false to me and you alone, the rare one, appeared true: like the many carved and painted shapes a master painter drew to catch a likeness, which to those who run their hands over them all without stopping show themselves as one wall.
verse.nuance: Two images carry the verse: the blind man for whom pit and road exchange places, which is the unenlightened state, and the painted wall, which is the enlightened one: the painter's many figures differ to the eye but the hand that feels them finds one surface, so the many things are false and the one substrate true. இல்லன உளவாய் உள்ளன காணா is the plain statement of maya in the Vedantic sense. The prose line printed after the verse (சடமாகிய உடம்பு எனக் கொண்டு, கல்லா உடம்பு எனவும் பாடமோதுவர்) is an editor's note that some read கல்லா உடம்பு for கல்லா உளத்தின்.

finding.claim: Nearly every cell keeps a roughly 24-hour molecular clock entrained by light, and misalignment of these clocks is linked to metabolic and mental illness.

verse.reading: The One that was in me I did not know; after I came to know the One in me, who else could see it? Staying and staying within myself, I perceived it.
verse.nuance: Line 3 can be read as 'who could see it (but I)?' or as 'who is able to see it?' in general. Either way the knowledge is in-dwelling and not transferable, and the verse gives no method beyond இருந்திருந்து, staying within.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: 'I will do alchemy: silver, and gold finer than the touchstone's gold'; saying 'give gold and coins enough for the guru's bundle', performing tricks and deceiving, they take the property that was handed over and run a league away; even catching sight of them again is rare.
verse.nuance: A plain account of the alchemist's confidence trick: the fee demanded in advance (குருமுடிச்சு, the guru's bundle) and the flight. The verse treats வாதம் (alchemy) as it is practised, a fraud, and says nothing about whether transmutation is possible.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: At sixteen he has the teaching of a guru of lofty wisdom and the arts of Tamil to their shore, is praised as a waxing moon, dresses his hair with flowers that bees hum round, wears gold and gems and is bowed to by bards; women see him as Kama's form, crowd and throw their curved glances, and when they go like peacocks he runs after them, embraces, drinks the nectar of their lips and gives away the whole capital he had gathered; the hoarded wealth is lost to idleness, and calling this the pleasure and grief of Kama he parts from the youthful form; prosperity and youth change, the strong teeth fall, the two eyes darken, age ripens, grey hair and wrinkles come with wind, quarrel and anger, and a staff is in his red hand.
verse.nuance: Learning and wealth are given to the youth only so that the women can strip them; the stanza does not call the women courtesans, but தேடிய மாமுதல் சேர வழங்கி (giving away all the capital he had sought) is the courtesan verses' plot. வாதவிரோதகுரோதம் can be read as the wind-disease of old age or as quarrelsomeness; தடி (staff) and நரைதிரை are the standard marks of age.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: It tells of the guru who is the place where pati is; do not open it in public, your head will split in two; listen as I say what place fate is: it is the uvula within the sky of the sky; moon and sun, pooranam, eye, mouth, nose, the great ear and touch, eight; the place where pati dwells, its name is the suzhumunai; they call it heaven and Kailasa.
verse.nuance: The verse names the place three ways: the uvula within the inner sky, the suzhumunai, and heaven and Kailasa, which 2439 expands into a list of all the holy places. The eight (moon, sun, pooranam and the five senses) is another of the run's counts. விதியின்ன விடம், 'the place where fate is', is strange; a variant sense is 'the place as ordained'. The threat that the head splits in two for telling it openly is a conventional curse on breaking secrecy.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: In the street of the crown's middle, in the kind that remained, the fresh moon spreading and sporting; the lamp that is vermilion, the silence that is meditation, the silence that is bound: Sivayam passed beyond.
verse.nuance: உச்சி மத்தி, the middle of the crown, is the highest centre. ஒழிந்திருந்த சாதி, the kind or caste that remained, is odd; it may mean what is left when all else is gone. செச்சி (vermilion, or the plant of that name) and கச்சி are rhyme words whose sense I cannot fix. கடந்ததே, passed beyond, closes the chapter.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Adorning the vessel, the women with hair unbound, not knowing the reckoning, Jnanam, mother, wept in confusion.
verse.nuance: The scene is a funeral: women loosen their hair in mourning. கலம் may be the pot or bier of the dead, or the body itself as a vessel; கணக்கு, the reckoning, is perhaps the count of days or deeds that the mourners never learned.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: It is done: all the diseases in the body fly away when an atom of it is eaten; body-siddhi has grown great and one can live joined to the substance; take the oil of the thalaippindam, of the creeper and of the mango; after taking the oil add camphor without hesitation and do pooja to the substance with joy.
verse.nuance: தலைப்பிண்டம் is unexplained (a plant? a prepared ball?); கொடியும் மாவும் may be plant names or a powder. வத்து, the substance, is worshipped, the alchemical product treated as the god, which 2401 continues.

finding.claim: Siddha polyherbal decoctions such as Nilavembu and Kaba Sura Kudineer have been tested in few, small COVID-19 trials, with uncertain benefit beyond standard care.

verse.reading: Will it be bound? At the gate of impurity, in the middle of the centre, by kundalini's vaasi, if one binds the eight and the four and reveres them, one can mount and ride.
verse.nuance: மலவாயில், the gate of impurity, is the body's lowest opening, so the centre is the muladhara of 2593. The eight and the four are not explained; tradition offers the eight petals and four petals of the lower lotuses, or the eight siddhis and four steps. The horse is bound where kundalini sleeps and ridden from there.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: So that the sorrow of my being born in a birth lower than a dog's ends, when will I shine like fire-light in bamboo?
verse.nuance: The fire latent in bamboo comes out by friction; the light is already in the poet's wretched birth. நாயிற் கடைப்பிறப்பு is the poet's self-abasement, a stance kept through the work.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: Without birth and death, without speech and breath, without forgetting and remembering, when will I be as one dead?
verse.nuance: மாண்டிருப்பது, to be dead, is asked for as a state while alive: the three pairs removed are the marks of ordinary life. The stopped breath (மூச்சும் அற்று) is the yogic sign of the state.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: In the chakra of the worlds, in the space of the lord of the elements, the wind packed within the fire of the swelling lamp; at the gate where the two, sun and moon, move, changing the staff and climbing up, in the sporting space ...
verse.nuance: The stanza has no finite verb and seems to be the first half of a sentence that 1291 finishes. தவன and சோமன், sun and moon, are the right and left channels on the yogic reading tradition gives; தண்டு, the staff, is the spine; the space where the two play is the central channel. The wind packed in fire is the breath held at the root.

tamil: ஊன் நிறைந்த காயம் உயிர் இழந்து போகுமுன்னம்
நான் இறந்து போக இனி நாள் வருவது எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will the day come for me to die, before this body full of flesh loses its life and goes?
verse.nuance: A plain restatement of 89 with the body as ஊன் நிறைந்த காயம், the flesh-filled frame. நான் இறந்து போக is the death of the 'I', not of the body, which has its own later death.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: It burns in the fire, it is burnt and turns to powder and ash, alas for me, sinner: the hand that cherished me and raised me, that dandled me so that the great bird would not fly away.
verse.nuance: மாகக் குருவி பறவாமல், so that the sky-bird would not fly, is read as the mother guarding the infant's life (உயிர் as a bird that may leave the body), an image the Kural also uses; it may instead be a lullaby's bird. The verse watches a single part, the hand, go to ash.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: Listen, son Vasimuni: in the thousand verses he gave earlier he told truly the drugs, salts, bound and melted substances and the way of gems, without a lie; in this book he will tell all the silence in order, so listen bowing.
verse.nuance: The disciple is வாசிமுனி, the breath-sage, and later வாசிநாதா; the name makes the pupil the breath itself. The earlier ஆயிரம் is an alchemical work claimed as Kakapusundar's; the verse marks the turn from alchemy to மவுனம், which the formulas of 2397 to 2403 then undo.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: I will not grieve, dying and being born along the way of the deluding senses; I will not join that way and so do not enter birth; having scooped and eaten the great honey of famous Marudur, I stayed with no desire for anything else, and now I will not go and beg anything from anyone.
verse.nuance: பெருந்தேன் முகந்து உண்டு, scooping and eating the great honey, is the poet's figure for the taste of the Lord that ends wanting; the venba before promised everything to those who say the name, and this verse answers that there is nothing left to want. இரவேன் ஒருவரை, I will not beg from anyone, is the Kural's language of இரவு turned to the mendicant poet's one refusal.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: Poor heart, who with sidelong glances falling on the heavy breasts in the bodice stands in desire: stitch yourself to the feet of him who shares his side with Unnamulai, the fresh green creeper borne of Himavan; mind, there is never any fault in that.
verse.nuance: The remedy for desire for a woman's breast is the goddess Unnamulai (she of the unsuckled breast) at Siva's side, so the verse answers lust with the one female figure it will allow. தைச்சுக்கிட, sew yourself in, is a strong image of attachment transferred rather than removed.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: Desire for the womb does not die; your life is impermanent; is there in that honey-pot a bliss beyond pleasure? In small pleasure, when the flesh is gone and the body is gone and goes, knowing nothing, for the low there is no heaven but the burning ground.
verse.nuance: சுகாதீதம், beyond pleasure, is the word for the bliss of release; the verse asks whether sex gives it and answers with the burning ground. The target is lust alone; the body's other appetites are not mentioned.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: When will I have died already, before the soul in its cage falls dead, slowly, as with a yawn?
verse.nuance: கூண்டு, the cage, is the body; the yawn (கொட்டாவி) is the slow last breath. To die before dying is the Siddhar's state of the living dead, the self already gone while the body stands, taken up again at 90, 126 and 139.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: Saying that in every land and time we shall remain without dying, and not looking closely at you, the poet says he lost his form.
verse.nuance: இறவாதிருப்பம், we shall not die, is the unspoken belief of ordinary life put into words; உருவழிந்தேன், lost my form, is the plain answer, the body gone. The stanza may also be read as a jibe at those who seek deathlessness in the wrong place, since 968 and 1033 claim it from the breath.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: In that which, as awareness here and as knowledge there, filled and became everything everywhere, heart, you were made one.
verse.nuance: ஏகரித்தாய், you made one or became one, is the verb of union used again at 782. The pervading thing is described as உணர்வு and அறிவு, feeling-awareness and knowledge, not as a God; the work never names Siva.

finding.claim: Loophole-free Bell tests confirm that entangled particles show correlations no local hidden-variable theory can explain, though these cannot be used to send signals.

verse.reading: He of unchanging fame and the honey garland, the Siva-yogi of silence who does not open his mouth to rage; and straight (2197) his guru is Chitrambalavan.
verse.nuance: வாய்திறந்து சீறாத: silence is defined as not opening the mouth in anger, a narrower and more practical mounam than the stilling of all thought. Yet 2194 gave him fury; the anger is turned on the disciples' enemies, not spoken.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: One must win the boon of not being born; and having been born, there is a medicine for not dying, see how it is: heart, do not forget the lotus feet of the Lord of the dharma-rich hall of Tillai; see, that is the good medicine for you.
verse.nuance: இறவாதிருக்க மருந்து, a medicine against dying, is the Siddhars' promise, usually kept by breath or kalpa herbs; Pattinathar names remembrance of the feet as the drug. Whether the deathlessness is bodily or the end of rebirth is not said.

finding.claim: Artemisinin, isolated from sweet wormwood after a search of traditional Chinese recipes, became a frontline malaria drug, showing traditional texts can point to real compounds.

verse.reading: Did I do japa and tapas only to lose the body? And what if one does yoga alone? Consider it, stony mind.
verse.nuance: The verse is two questions and the stance is unclear. On one reading japa and tapas wear the body away while yoga keeps it, so yoga is preferred (the kaya siddhi view); on another, even yoga alone is not enough, and the mind must weigh what each yields.

finding.claim: Much meditation research suffers from vague definitions, small samples and overstated claims, and the evidence for its benefits is weaker than popular accounts suggest.

verse.reading: Fly, dragonfly, and say that every thing is a dream, that all the world will perish, that the body is a letter written on water and that only the First is without end.
verse.nuance: அப்பில் எழுத்து, writing on water, is the verse's own image for the body's impermanence; the gloss confirms அப்பு as water. The stanza sets three perishables against one imperishable, ஆதி, and that contrast is the whole argument.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: The thought that runs about: catch it without letting it run, gather it and set it right; seek, and fit it to the arrow; set it within the wide open space of nada's end.
verse.nuance: அம்பு, the arrow, recurs in 2287 (அம்பு பூணும்); tradition reads it as the fixed inward gaze or the straight breath. நாதாந்த வெட்டவெளி, the bare open space at the end of sound, is where the mind is to be lodged; the stanza is the song's one positive method, framed in the same imperatives as its prohibitions.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: It must not be said, demon; even if said, it is a fault; no, no: you have seen solitude.
verse.nuance: தோடம் is தோஷம், a fault; speaking of the real is one. இல்லை இல்லை, 'no, no', is the stanza's only content, and ஏகாந்தம் (solitude, aloneness) names the state left when speech stops.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Above the Avyakrita who holds the eggs, above Hiranyagarbha who is Vishnu, above the lightning-bright Virat Purusha, above these there is consciousness.
verse.nuance: வியாகிருதன், இரணியகர்ப்பன் and விராட் புருடன் are the three cosmic selves of Vedanta, presiding over the universe's deep sleep, dream and waking; the kummi equates Hiranyagarbha with Vishnu. இண்டமுண்ட is garbled, perhaps அண்டமுண்ட (who swallowed the eggs). சைதன்னியம் (chaitanya), consciousness, is above all three and is named Brahman in 2611.

finding.claim: An underground radiation experiment ruled out the simplest parameter-free version of the gravity-related collapse model that Orch-OR depends on.

verse.reading: You people confused by the mantras you have learned, will you recite them when you are dead? The mantras are within you, and so are you who valued them; the mantra is the five letters of the mind.
verse.nuance: The second line is the hinge: a mantra held in memory dies with the one who learned it. மனத்தின் ஐந்து எழுத்து relocates the pancakshara from speech to the mind, which the rest of the chapter develops.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: Having done pooja, preserve it well; take the oil of the wild ridge-gourd, the oils of asaipul and manakkathuvu likewise, add the ghee of kesari, add the bile of the slender loris, add the oil of the thalaippindam, grind it without speaking, son, and add civet and musk.
verse.nuance: A compounding of oils, biles and perfumes, read here for what it claims rather than as a method: the brow-collyrium of 2402. பேய்ப்பீர்க்கு is the wild ridge-gourd; ஆசைபுல், மணக்கதுவு and தலைப்பிண்டம் are not identified; கேசரி may be lion or saffron. பாசையடா பேசாமல், grinding without speaking, is a rite condition.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: There is a root in the house, and in the forest outside is Tirumular; for the great ones who are caught in it, is this not rasavada, girl of knowledge?
verse.nuance: The stanza puns on மூலம்: the herb-root sought in the forest, the மூலாதாரம் at the base of the body that is 'in the house', and திருமூலர், the Siddha whose name is the 'holy root'. The plain sense is that the root for alchemy is at home; the coded sense is that the true rasavada is the root centre, as Tirumular taught.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: Om: listen, pupil of ruined mind; in the world a man's years are a hundred; is it not twenty-one thousand six hundred breaths in a day? Because they went, going out with the breath, the days diminished and were gone; if they do not go out, there is no going; when a man thinks one thing, the god thinks it too; are not fates only what one has thought?
verse.nuance: The breath-count of 21,600 a day is the standard figure of the hatha texts (fifteen a minute), and the verse's arithmetic is the Siddhar theory of life: a life is a fixed number of breaths, so the breath held is life saved. The last two lines go further and make விதி (fate) the product of one's own thought, with the god only concurring.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: When one drinks the honey that is the kalpa called self, its name is sanchara samadhi; the flesh's hunger ends and anger goes; going to the hill of rising and piercing through, the seven screens called honey burn away; for those who go to the centre of the crown all the instruments called king subside and one can watch Death's dance.
verse.nuance: சஞ்சார சமாதி, the samadhi of moving about, is the siddha's waking absorption (also 2376). உதயகிரி, the hill of rising, is a cipher for the crown or the brow. கூற்றுவனாராட்டம் can mean watching Yama's play from safety or seeing Death's dance ended; the sense turns on whether ஆட்டம் is defeat or performance.

finding.claim: Maximum human lifespan appears to have plateaued near 115-125 years, and radical life extension in this century is judged implausible.
